topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the cancer course context, sets out the questions surrounding cancer causation, and outlines the session's learning objectives.

topics.label: Concepts and Epidemiology of Cancer Causation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish cancer as a multifactorial genetic disease by evaluating the relative contributions of intrinsic biological errors, inherited risk, and environmental exposures evidenced through population epidemiology.

topics.label: Pathogen-Driven Carcinogenesis and Burkitt Lymphoma
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how infectious agents promote oncogenesis, using the discovery and molecular etiology of Burkitt lymphoma as a primary case study.

topics.label: Mechanisms of Chemical and Physical Carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how physical radiation and chemical compounds interact with cellular processes and xenobiotic metabolism to cause DNA damage and mutations.

topics.label: Tumor Promotion, Inflammation, and Host Susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore non-mutagenic mechanisms of cancer development, focusing on inflammatory tumor promoters, tissue microenvironments, and developmental stages of host vulnerability.

topics.label: Methodologies for Detecting and Proving Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics review the analytical tools, population biobanks, animal models, and in vitro assays used to identify mutational signatures and test whether agents cause cancer.

topics.label: Concluding Summary and Risk-Benefit Considerations
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the session by summarizing the central themes of the lecture and discussing real-world risk-benefit evaluations regarding carcinogen exposures.
